question: Under which Article does the Supreme Court of India exercise original jurisdiction in cases involving the violation of Fundamental Rights?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 32**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

 
• **Article 32** of the Indian Constitution empowers the Supreme Court to enforce Fundamental Rights through appropriate writs.
 
• It is referred to as the "**Right to Constitutional Remedies**" and is considered the soul of the Constitution, as described by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
 
• The Supreme Court can issue five types of writs under Article 32: **Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, and Quo Warranto**.
 
• This article provides individuals the right to directly approach the Supreme Court
